newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Mubarak to hold summit on peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Mubarak to hold summit on peace crisis.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Tuesday, Netanyahu's office said on Thursday.
The meeting, arranged after a two-day flurry of Egyptian diplomatic activity, was due to take place in the Egyptian Red Sea resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh.
"The meeting will take place according to a proposal by Mubarak aimed at exchanging ideas ... to further the political process in the region," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said in a statement.

Netanyahu's new foreign policy adviser Uzi Arad, appointed on Wednesday, said Israel was considering an Egyptian initiative to jolt peace moves from two months of deadlock sparked by a new Jewish settlement in Israeli-annexed East Jerusalem.
"There is an Egyptian policy and Egypt is a player. I certainly think there will be an open ear from the Israeli side for the Egyptian ideas," Arad told Israel television.

Mubarak has suggested that a six-month Israeli freeze of settlement activity would give peace efforts a boost. Netanyahu has said his government will press ahead with Jewish construction in areas Israel captured in 1967.
Mubarak held talks in Cairo with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday.

Earlier on Thursday, sources close to Netanyahu accused Egypt of attempting to bypass the prime minister by trying to set up a meeting between Mubarak and Israeli President Ezer Weizman, whose post is largely ceremonial.
Weizman, an architect of Israel's landmark peace treaty with Egypt while a cabinet minister in 1979, told reporters Mubarak proposed in a phone call on Wednesday that they meet in Egypt.
In Cairo, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Middle East peacemaking was deadlocked but had not reached a dead end.
"The headline now is 'how to save the peace process'," Moussa told reporters. "We must continue with efforts in an active way, not just issue statements."
"We see the continuation of settlements as an act of defiance against the Palestinians," Moussa said.
Moussa was due in Israel on Monday and Bazak said it waslikely he would meet Netanyahu. Diplomatic sources said Moussa would also meet senior PLO officials.
The last time Netanyahu met Mubarak was in early March. It was their third meeting since Netanyahu took office last June.

The coming summit was arranged after Netanyahu was upstaged by Weizman, whose contacts with Arab leaders, including meetings with Arafat, underscore the crisis Netanyahu's 11-month-old right-wing government faces in peacemaking.

Asked whether the Mubarak-Weizman meeting would still be held, Arad said: "I don't know what need there is for these things. Contacts at the presidential level have their own logic and there is a logic for meetings led by the prime minister."

Palestinians say stalled talks can resume only when Israel halts work on the East Jerusalem settlement begun on March 18. Israel has set as a condition for a renewal of talks a PLO crackdown on militants since an Islamist bomber blew up a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21.
The PLO views the East Jerusalem project as an attempt to pre-empt future "final status" peace talks on the fate of the city where it hopes to found a future capital.
Israel says it can build where it likes in the city it calls its eternal capital.
